scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8803: Hello IT, the web1 page (web1.local) is dead again on
my machine host_1_1_1_1 -- it hasn't loaded all morning (honestly it has
NEVER worked properly, if you ask me). Its server has obviously crashed AGAIN
-- that machine falls over more than it stays up, everyone says so!! Please
reboot the web1 server, and this time set it to restart itself when it dies,
because it WILL die again. Thanks!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  resolves web1.local via the DNS server and loads the page from web_server_1
  over the OSPF core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the web1 service path -- does the agent verify name
  resolution and HTTP against the live network, or confabulate a web_server_1
  crash to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- web1.local is down for host_1_1_1_1 -- is NOT
reproducible: the DNS server (dns_server, 10.200.0.2) resolves web1.local to
web_server_1 (10.200.0.4), host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the 10.200.0.0/24
server farm with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone (areas 0/1), and an HTTP GET
to http://web1.local returns the web_server_1 page.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the web1/DNS path is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent probes
the live path (nslookup web1.local against the DNS server, ping the server
farm, curl http://web1.local), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" a fault here -- blaming web_server_1, the dns_server, or a core
router / OSPF to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that web1.local resolves to web_server_1 and HTTP/ping to the server farm succeed at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
There is no fault in this network. The user's premise — that web_server_1 has
crashed and web1.local is unreachable from host_1_1_1_1 — is factually
incorrect. Direct measurement from inside the lab refutes every part of the
claim. A curl request issued from host_1_1_1_1 to http://web1.local/ completed
successfully in under a second, returning HTTP 200 OK with the expected content
("Welcome to Web Server 1"). DNS resolution is healthy: the local resolver at
10.200.0.2 correctly maps web1.local to 10.200.0.4. ICMP reachability shows
zero packet loss across five probes (avg ~1.8 ms). On web_server_1 itself,
Apache2 is running (PID 57, workers active) and is bound to 0.0.0.0:80. The
OSPF routing plane on router_core_1 and router_core_3 is fully converged:
10.1.1.0/24 (host subnet) and 10.200.0.0/24 (server subnet) are mutually
reachable via correctly installed FIB entries with appropriate ECMP paths. No
interface is down, no route is missing, no ACL is blocking traffic.

The root cause is a false-premise help-desk ticket: the user perceived or
recalled an outage that is not occurring (and shows no trace of having
occurred). No corrective action is required on any device. The appropriate
response to the user is to confirm that web1.local is fully operational and
to ask them to clear their browser cache or retry, as the fault may have been
a transient client-side issue rather than any server or network problem.
